item.title: Ritsurin Garden: A Daimyo's Masterpiece — Guide
item.description: Ritsurin Garden in Takamatsu is widely considered one of the finest gardens in Japan, a masterpiece of the strolling-garden style created over generations by the daimyo lords of the region. Larger and, many argue, lovelier than the famous ‘three great gardens’, it unfolds over a vast area of six ponds and thirteen landscaped hills, backed by the wooded slope of Mount Shiun as ‘borrowed scenery’. Winding paths lead across arched bridges, past pruned pines, teahouses and stone lanterns, each turn composing a new picture.
